Seminar Title:

Restoration of a long-standing partially failed pit slope located along the mine boundary

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Type:

Abstract:

Mine-boundary slopes that remain partially failed for prolonged periods can pose significant geotechnical, operational, environmental, and economic risks, while simultaneously restricting access to potentially valuable mineral resources. This study presents a comprehensive case study on the restoration and sustainable management of a long-standing partially failed pit slope along the boundary of an opencast iron ore mine. The investigation integrated field-based rock-mass mapping, geological discontinuity assessment, laboratory characterization, slope geometry evaluation, drainage considerations, and Limit Equilibrium Method (LEM)-based stability analysis. Multiple individual bench angles were evaluated to identify a safe and operationally suitable configuration. The analysis indicated an optimum bench angle of 80° and an overall pit slope angle of 43°, with calculated Factor of Safety (FoS) values ranging from 1.553 to 6.939 across the investigated sections. The restoration strategy incorporated slope reshaping, removal of weakened/weathered material, improved drainage, structural stabilization, erosion control, native vegetation and bio- restoration measures, together with systematic monitoring and review. A key outcome of the study is the recognition that the left-out mineralized slope along the mine boundary should be managed not merely as a residual or failed slope, but as a potential future mineral asset, subject to geotechnical, economic, regulatory, and mine-planning considerations. Accordingly, an integrated asset-management framework is proposed covering asset identification, condition assessment, planning and design, implementation, ecological restoration, monitoring, risk management, and value realization. The study demonstrates how systematic slope rehabilitation can simultaneously improve safety, stability, environmental performance, mine-life potential, and resource value, providing a practical framework for transforming a legacy slope hazard into a stable, resilient, and potentially valuable future mining asset.
